scope: Four robotics papers reviewed (three full texts and one publisher abstract/introduction), plus two foundational swarm optimization sources consulted. Not an exhaustive literature review.

papers.title: Smart Gait: A Gait Optimization Framework for Hexapod Robots
papers.venue: Chinese Journal of Mechanical Engineering 37 article 15
papers.reviewed_version: Version of record 2024; cross-checked accessible 2023 preprint
papers.summary: Optimizes swing trajectories, gait period and duty, and online leg-lifting sequences on LittleStrong. Offline dynamics-based trajectory/timing optimization feeds an online gait adapter and whole-body controller. The reported 15.9% improvement belongs to its period/duty comparison and is not a promised battery saving for this robot.
papers.adaptation: Expose period, duty, lift and trajectory controls; run a separate matched gait sweep; measure positive mechanical actuator work and tilt/support/contact signals. Call this Smart-Gait-inspired parameter tuning, not a reproduction.
not_reproduced: Online gait adapter and whole-body control
limitations: Assisted body control changes balance and effort
Mechanical work and torque-squared effort are not electrical battery energy

papers.title: Hexapod robot motion planning investigation under the influence of multi-dimensional terrain features
papers.summary: Combines elevation and semantic terrain maps. Footprint-scale windows extract slope, height range, undulation and physical terrain properties for traversal-cost A*. A smaller foothold-cost map and free gait planner support local foot placement. The tested thresholds are platform-specific.
papers.adaptation: Create a terrain-aware A* baseline from existing scene height and terrain labels. Keep geometric hazard exposure separate from measured instability; label modeled friction or softness assumptions.
limitations: Current scene has no deformable mud or sand
Paper has equation/notation ambiguities; do not silently claim exact formula equivalence
Robot footprint and thresholds must be recalibrated

papers.title: Energy-Aware Planning for Delivery Tasks Executed by Legged Robots
papers.reviewed_version: Publisher abstract and introduction; author/DOI metadata cross-checked with Crossref
papers.summary: The accessible publisher abstract describes hierarchical energy-aware delivery planning. It compares graph-search instances involving battery replacement, payload splitting and speed reduction to minimize delivery completion time. Full equations and experimental details were not accessible in this review.
papers.adaptation: Use explicit battery and safe charger-return constraints plus separately configured service downtime. This is a generic energy-aware baseline inspired by the abstract, not an implementation of the paper.
not_reproduced: Exact energy model and graph formulation
limitations: Full text still required for faithful reproduction
Charging stops are not physical battery swaps
Current demonstration charge rate is accelerated

papers.title: STATE-NAV: Stability-Aware Traversability Estimation for Bipedal Navigation on Rough Terrain
papers.venue: arXiv 2506.01046v4; author record states accepted to IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters
papers.summary: TravFormer learns Digit-specific instability and uncertainty from terrain patches and velocity commands. A risk-sensitive bound selects fast admissible linear/angular commands. TravRRT* minimizes estimated traversal time, and bipedal MPC constrains execution. The authors evaluate MuJoCo and physical Digit navigation.
papers.adaptation: Collect hexapod terrain/speed response data and select conservative speeds from an empirical table. Until calibrated, call risk a terrain proxy. Keep the existing waypoint controller; do not call it TravFormer or bipedal MPC.
limitations: BSFA and biped stability limits do not transfer directly to six legs
The live author repository has later A* updates; pin the version when reproducing

papers.title: Particle Swarm Optimization
papers.summary: Foundational personal-best and swarm-best velocity and position updates.
papers.adaptation: Continuous random keys select waypoints in a safe A* seeded route corridor. Fitness is feasibility first, followed by a common distance time energy and terrain score.
limitations: A path-refinement adaptation, not an unseeded global planner.
Corridor choices are restricted to subsequences of the seed.

papers.title: Ant Colony System A Cooperative Learning Approach to the Traveling Salesman Problem
papers.summary: Foundational pheromone-mediated construction of discrete solutions. The author bibliography distinguishes Ant System and ACS variants.
papers.adaptation: An elitist Ant-System-style ACO constructs routes on forward visible chords, with probabilistic pheromone/heuristic choices, evaporation and deposits. This is not exact ACS and does not reproduce the TSP experiments.
not_reproduced: ACS q0 policy and local pheromone updates
limitations: Safe A* seed and finite forward corridor restrict global route exploration.
